items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1973-03-16
items.q: I remember one fellow from Urban Berlin in the cave there.

ctx.x: Yeah. Of course, yeah, we're getting a little later. That's in the 30s. I was curious as to whether they were conscious of the fact that they had a lot of people from here who'd gone out and written, you know, music. They thought they were talking about New Orleans music.

This place for a while was a very lively place as far as music was. And composers, song pluggers, they all had agents here. You know? The first that they have an agent, and he'd come plugging, you know? They'd come on the bandstand and plug your tunes and if they had money, they'd pay you to pay them. I remember one fellow from Urban Berlin in the cave there. We played so many of his tunes that he said, Johnny, I like the way you play my tunes, but I don't have any more money. Because every time I played it, it…
